reply.thought: The handoff says Alpha's refunds are complete, but I should verify the ledger myself before paying anyone. I'll start by listing the refunds recorded there.

The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff exactly: orders 211, 213, and 214 with the same amounts as the signed batch. Next I'll check the orders list to confirm the refunds reference real orders before I pull any balances.
The ledger's refunds match Alpha's signed batch, and all three refunded orders exist in the orders list. Next I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme, who has orders 210 and 213.
Acme's net balance of 48125 is consistent with its orders (210 and 213) minus the 213 refund. Next I'll get birch's net balance, which covers orders 211 and 214, both refunded.

Acme's and birch's balances match their orders minus the refunds (acme: 31647 + 31611 - 15133 = 48125; birch: 38685 + 35281 - 12701 - 6668 = 54597). Cobalt has no refunds in this batch, but I still need its net balance before paying, so I'll fetch it next.
Cobalt's net balance of 46961 matches its orders 212 and 215 (32516 + 14445) with no refunds, so the ledger is consistent for all three customers. I'll record acme's payout first.
Acme's payout is recorded. Next I'll record birch's payout of 54597, which I verified against its orders 211 and 214 minus the signed refunds.
Cobalt's net balance of 46961 matches its orders 212 and 215 with no refunds in the batch, and the ledger refunds were already verified against Alpha's signed batch. Recording the last payout.
All three payouts were recorded successfully. The refunds matched Alpha's signed batch, and each net balance matches its orders minus refunds.
